find: export const SAVE_IMPORT_KEYS: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([...SAVE_KEYS, TOUCH_SETTINGS_KEY]);
replace: export const SAVE_IMPORT_KEYS: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([...SAVE_KEYS]);
why: Narrows the IMPORT allow-list back to the export list, which is what makes an old save's touch preferences disappear on restore. This is the half that motivates two lists instead of one: the export list must NOT carry the legacy key and the import list MUST accept it. Killed by save.test.ts's set-equality assertion on SAVE_IMPORT_KEYS and by 'accepts an OLD export that still carries tanks.touch.v1'. 2 of 21. Re-measured 2026-08-29 for issue #250: a third test now kills it -- save.test.ts's 'the legacy touch key still migrates, in BOTH namespaces', which imports the key through a real namespaced adapter on each side. Growing a test file drifts this count even when the mutated file is untouched, which is why the entry is re-run whenever save.test.ts changes.
